title: Presshammer: HammerBERT & PressRL
summary: Research project exploring Rowhammer and Rowpress attacks on DRAM, including PoCs and AI-based solutions.
description:
This project was developed as my final year thesis and focuses on the conceptual combination of Rowhammer and Rowpress attacks to induce bit flips in DRAM. It features multiple proof-of-concept implementations that explore the feasibility and impact of these attacks across different scenarios.

The main contribution is HammerBERT, a Transformer-based (BERT) code analysis tool designed to classify code as malicious, benign, or neutral, making it particularly suitable for static application security testing (SAST). Additionally, PressRL is a reinforcement learning model aimed at mitigating risks by preventing unsafe open-row durations in memory systems, although it remains more conceptual compared to HammerBERT.

title: AIM
summary: Modular malware analysis framework combining traditional tools, AI agents, and automated reporting.
description:
AIM is a modular framework for malware analysis that integrates traditional analysis tools, AI agents, and automated reporting into a unified workflow. It provides a flexible architecture for building analysis pipelines, orchestrating tasks across different stages of the malware lifecycle, and assisting analysts with investigation and documentation.

Currently under development.
